newsitem.title: LATVIA: Nomura, EBRD may invest in Latvian Shipping Co.
newsitem.headline: Nomura, EBRD may invest in Latvian Shipping Co.

text.p: Japan's Nomura and the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) may buy stakes in the state-owned Latvian Shipping Company, the Latvian Privatization Agency (LPA) said on Wednesday.

"Among the companies interested in the first stake offered in the Latvian Shipping Company are the EBRD and Nomura International as well as several shipping companies," LPA director general Janis Naglis told a news conference.
"Nomura has also offered to quote shares of the shipping company on various stock markets around the world."
Proposals for participating in the privatization of the shipping firm are to be submitted to the LPA by November 1.
The Baltic state's government plans eventually to reduce its stake in the company to five percent.
Naglis said that a recent audit conducted by accountancy firm Coopers & Lybrand ranked the Latvian Shipping Company as the 19th largest in the world.
"The base capital of the company at the end of 1995 was $464.4 million," said Latvian Shipping director Peteris Avotins.
He added that the company, with a fleet of 74 ships, posted a $51 million loss in 1995 compared with a $29 million loss in 1994.
